title: Major Club women’s limited-over tournament National players take limelight | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 11:00
-     - 5

Vishmi Gunaratne’s brilliant 132 helped CCC defeat Navy SC, Harshitha Samarawickrama scored 87 in Navy SC’s run chase, Kaveesha Dilhari led Badureliya CC’s run spree with 102*, Shehara Induwari ran through the Ace Capital CC batting taking 7/10

National players came to the fore in the Major Club women’s limited-over match between CCC and Navy SC played at Welisara yesterday which the former won by eight runs (DLS method).

Vishmi Gunaratne hit a brilliant 132 off 142 balls (15 fours, 3 sixes) for CCC to reach 221-7 in 48 overs. Inoka Ranaweera picked up 3/34. Navy SC made a tremendous effort to reach their revised target of 221 off 41 overs through half-centuries from Harshitha Samarawickrama (87 off 91 balls, 11 fours, 1 six) and Hasini Perera (57 off 79 balls, 7 fours) who put on 125 for the second wicket only to fall short by nine runs.   

Badureliya CC went to the top of the Group B standings with a comprehensive 202-run win (DLS method) over Ace Capital CC at SLLDC grounds, Maggona. Skipper Kaveesha Dilhari led Badureliya CC’s run spree of 212-5 in 41 overs scoring a fabulous century (102* off 85 balls, 11 fours) supported by Sanjana Kavindi (50 off 98 balls, 3 fours). Ace Capital CC chasing a revised target of 236 slumped to 33-9 in 13.5 overs falling to the off-breaks of Shehara Induwari (7/10). – [ST]

Major Club Women’s Limited-Over tournament SSC tops table with second successive win

Malsha Madushani, a grand all-round performance for SSC (28* & 2/9)

SSC went to the top of the Major Club Women’s limited-over Group B table when they secured their second successive win beating Chilaw Marians CC by eight wickets at the DHH grounds, Madampella yesterday.

Chilaw Marians CC were shot out for 58 in 34.5 overs with right-arm seamers Achini Kulasuriya (3/10) and Malsha Madushani (2/9) being the main destroyers. SSC romped home in 9.2 overs scoring 59-2 with Madushani displaying her all-round prowess by scoring an unbeaten 28 off 25 balls (4 fours, 1 six). [ST]

title: Tier B 50-over tournament  Army SC, Galle CC, Chilaw Marians CC, Navy SC maintain unbeaten record | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:56
-     - 5

Army SC, Galle CC, Chilaw Marians CC and Navy SC maintained their unbeaten record in the Tier B 50-over tournament with facile wins in their respective matches played on Thursday.

Army SC registered the most convincing of wins crushing Kandy Customs SC by a massive 194 runs under the DLS method at Panagoda. Half-centuries from Ashan Sudarshana (53 off 68 balls, 6 fours, 1 six), Pathum Dilshan (67 off 92 balls, 6 fours, 1 six) and Asela Gunaratne (53 off 37 balls, 8 fours) saw Army SC rattle off 280-8 and then rout Kandy Customs SC for 67 with spinners Shehada Zoysa (5/19) and Lilan Rangana (3/18) sharing the spoils.

Galle CC thumped Sebastianites by eight wickets at Surrey grounds, Maggona with a strong batting display. Galle CC overhauled Sebastianites’ total of 204 replying with 208-2 the major part of their run chase being handled by former Mahinda College, Galle cricketer Dulsith Darshana who hit an unbeaten 104 off 153 balls (12 fours, 2 sixes) and shared an opening stand of 114 with Yuthika de Silva (58 off 55 balls, 6 fours, 1 six). Only Teron Baskaran (75 off 71 balls, 8 fours, 1 six) stood tall for Sebastianites against the pace cum spin attack of Kavindu Nirmana (4/33) and Chanaka Devinda (3/42).

Chilaw Marians CC coasted to a four-wicket win against United Southern SC at the Mahinda Rajapaksa Stadium, Hambantota. A century opening stand of 110 by Arosha Sithumina (46) and Eshan Withanage (55 off 83 balls, 4 fours) saw Chilaw Marians CC reach their target of 211 with seven balls to spare. Former Matara Thomians captain Pesandu Sanjan took 4/35 with spin. For United Southern SC, Kavindu Ediriweera top scored with 72 off 101 balls (3 fours).

Navy SC pulled off a comfortable 28-run win against Kurunegala SC at Welisara. Although the winning margin looked small, Navy SC were in total control of the chase, reducing Kurunegala SC to 162-7. Only a 70-run stand off 72 balls between Sanuja Ninduwara (51 of 47 balls, 2 fours, 3 sixes) and skipper Sarinda Dassanayake (27) delayed the inevitable. Two half-century stands featured Navy SC’s innings of 269 – 80 between Pulasthi Athapaththu (17) and Thimira Malshan (63 off 72 balls, 3 fours, 3 sixes) and 68 between Avindu Theekshana (48) and Ishan Abeysekara (35). The spin and pace of Ruchira Silva (4/45) and Sanuja Ninduwara (3/77) accounted for the wickets.

Moratuwa SC and Negombo CC recorded their first wins. Moratuwa SC beat Ragama CC by 134 runs (DLS method) at SLLDC grounds Kirimandala. Chamara Fernando (59 off 52 balls, 1 fours, 5 sixes) top scored in Moratuwa SC’s total of 268-9. Ragama CC chasing a revised target of 245 was put out for 110 by seamer Mayura Malshan (3/25) and spinners Madusanka Premarathna (3/19) and Rusith Jayawardana (2/12).

Negombo CC defended their moderate total of 205 by dismissing Leo CC for 119 and win by 86 runs at Air Force grounds, Katunayake. Thathsara Eshan top scored for Negombo CC with 71 off 77 balls (5 fours) and left-arm spinner Sudara Dakshina claimed 5/44. Hansaja Hiruna, Amitha Sandeepa and Shehan Pramod took three wickets apiece. [ST]

title: Cristiano Ronaldo hints at retirement at end of season | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 18 August 2026 10:55
-     - 7

Cristiano Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo ‌‌has fuelled speculation about his retirement plans after saying ⁠⁠the upcoming ⁠⁠year will probably be the last of his playing career.

The 41-year-old Portugal captain is one of the ⁠⁠most decorated players of all time, winning major trophies with Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and current club ⁠⁠Al-Nassr since making his senior debut for Sporting in 2002.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner was unable to add a World Cup title to his list of honours after Portugal fell ‌‌short at this year’s tournament, leaving the sport’s biggest prize absent from his trophy cabinet.

“This is probably my last year of football and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo told lifestyle magazine Vogue in an interview published on Sunday.

The forward has scored 976 ⁠⁠goals for club and country during a ⁠⁠career spanning more than two decades.

“I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard. Because ⁠⁠football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ⁠⁠ways, not just one,” he said.

“And ⁠⁠also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I’ve earned—what we’ve earned. Because, after ‌‌all, it’s been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice.”

Ronaldo will continue playing for Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr ‌‌this ‌‌season as he closes in on the milestone of 1,000 career goals.
